NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using vibration analysis as the leading indicator for gearbox wear. Our departure is a same-class mechanism using torque harmonic distortion analysis from existing motor current and encoder data to detect raceway wear and grease degradation. This works because wear introduces asymmetric friction and compliance variations that generate specific torque harmonics not present in healthy operation.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: Torque ripple harmonics are generated by the nonlinear contact forces in the gearbox. As the raceway wears, the contact geometry changes, introducing higher-order harmonics in the torque transfer. The magnitude of the 5th harmonic component (5× fundamental frequency) is expected to increase by at least 15dB when wear reaches the critical threshold. This is CALCULATED based on tribological studies of cycloidal gear wear patterns and their effect on force transmission.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Data acquisition system (already-existing motor current and encoder signals)
- Digital signal processing unit (extracts torque harmonics from current data)
- Encoder data processing (calculates actual output position vs commanded position)
- Harmonic analysis algorithm (computes 5th harmonic amplitude from torque signal)
- Threshold comparison module (compares harmonic amplitude against critical value)
- Alert generation system (triggers warning when threshold exceeded)

Input streams:
- Motor current (ALREADY-RECORDED per "existing motor current/torque")
- Encoder position data (ALREADY-RECORDED per "existing encoder")

Reference/threshold:
- Critical harmonic amplitude threshold (CALCULATED from stated physical relation: 15dB increase from baseline healthy harmonic level)
- Baseline harmonic signature (DERIVED from stated specs: healthy gearbox harmonic signature at operating conditions)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensor connections, no additional hardware required
- Operability: SAME - operates continuously in background, no additional operator intervention
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance required beyond standard motor maintenance
- Cost class: SAME - software-only solution, no additional hardware costs
- False alarm rate: DESIGNED to meet <=1 false alarm per 100 robots/yr through harmonic specificity

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Monitor 100 robots in service for 12 months, recording motor current and encoder data continuously. Apply the harmonic analysis algorithm to detect the 5th harmonic component increase. When harmonic amplitude exceeds threshold by 15dB, record as positive prediction. Compare prediction timing against actual path error measurements taken weekly.

Instruments: Existing motor current sensors and encoders, data acquisition system, path error measurement equipment.

Pass/fail thresholds: 
- Must achieve >=30 days advance warning of path error exceeding spec
- Must maintain <=1 false alarm per 100 robots/yr
- Must detect all actual failures (no misses)

Duration: 12 months of continuous monitoring.

Kill criterion: If any robot experiences path error exceeding spec without prior warning, or if false alarm rate exceeds 1 per 100 robots/yr, the predictor is invalidated.

Validation: Test will be validated against ALREADY-RECORDED data from historical robot performance records and stated path error specifications.
